titleEn: Even in the Dark, the Lighthouse Turns!

pages.text: "Dad, do not turn off the lamp!" Lolo pulled the covers up to their nose with both hands. Dad's hand paused over the window lamp. In the next bed, Riri hung her yellow hat on a post.
Dad blew out the lamp. The room went dark. "I do not like the dark. Turn it on again." Lolo's voice grew thin—though by day, Lolo splashed bravely into waves.
Something big and pointed stood against the wall. "Wh-what is that?" Lolo squeezed their eyes shut, pulling even the toes under the covers.
Dad sat beside the bed and held Lolo's hand. "That scared you. Lolo, can you look at the window?" "It is dark. What is there to see...?" Lolo opened their eyes just a little.
Just then, white light swept through the window. The pointed thing lit up. Dad's raincoat on a hook! "Oh? It was not a monster!" Lolo's eyes opened wide.
"The lighthouse light turns around and around. Wait, and it comes back," Dad whispered. "Even in the dark, the lighthouse turns!" Lolo watched the window. Sweep—the light returned!
"I will count," Riri said, spreading her fingers. "One, two, three!" On three, light passed and brightened a corner. "Those are my boots!" Lolo laughed.
Lolo sat up out of the covers. Each time the light passed, the room grew bright. "Dark just means the light is off!"
Dad taught three things to do when scared. "One, say you are scared! Two, wait for the light! Three, hold the hand beside you!" Riri reached between their beds.
Dad hugged Lolo, covers and all. "Knowing how to wait makes even a dark night less scary." Holding Riri's hand, Lolo yawned. "Even in the dark, the lighthouse turns!"
